title: "Held" (an erase held undrawn) is derived in two places with different checks
evidence: Checkpoint 4 look-back. The held state is drawn nil, problem nil, recordJSON not empty. ios/HealthRoadmap/MyData/RecordStore.swift:399 applyInTurn refuses on predatesErase || (drawn == nil && problem == nil), with no recordJSON check. PR 1681 (S45) changes redraw (RecordStore.swift:263-270 today, which guards drawn != nil at :265) to guard drawn != nil || (problem == nil && !recordJSON.isEmpty && !predatesErase), around :266 after it lands. Two readings of one question that can drift apart: the first also refuses a store with no record loaded (recordJSON empty), the second does not count that as held. Fix: one named computed property on RecordStore (for example isHeldUndrawn), read by both; or keep the hold in the Source state (RecordStore+Source.swift:8) so it is one named state, not three fields. Same family as S55 (the no-writable-record rule in three places): do them together. US-25 AC16f | in progress (PR 1684): one named property, RecordStore.heldUndrawn (RecordStore+Readable.swift: drawn nil, problem nil, recordJSON not empty, not predatesErase). redraw reads drawn != nil || heldUndrawn; applyInTurn reads predatesErase || heldUndrawn || (drawn == nil && problem == nil && recordJSON.isEmpty), the last term keeping its refusal of a store with no record yet. Both equal the old conditions on all 16 inputs (checked by hand and by an exhaustive script in review, not by a test); HeldUndrawnTableTests.swift pins heldUndrawn's 16 rows as literals. US-25 AC16f S55 not built: the property is its first piece.
